MSM8996 native-SMD RPM logical-corner resource
============================================

This frontend implements the Sony MSM8996 corn/vfc/swen apps-master requests.
It is NOT a physical microvolt regulator. The legacy regulator voltage API and
regulator-min/max-microvolt property names carry logical corners 1..7 ONLY for
this explicit compatible/use-voltage-corner contract. Firmware receives corn
or vfc value logical-1 (0..6), never a uv KVP. Do not connect ordinary physical
voltage consumers or native microvolt S1/S2 providers to these supplies.

Resource required properties:
- compatible: "qcom,msm8996-rpm-corner-resource"
- qcom,rpm: phandle to the real qcom,rpm-msm8996 request node
- qcom,resource-name and qcom,resource-id: "smpa"/1 (CX), "smpa"/2 (MX),
  or "ldoa"/26 (original SS-CX corner resource). No other resources supported.

Every available child must have:
- compatible: "qcom,rpm-smd-regulator"
- regulator-name: unique frontend name
- qcom,set: 1 ACTIVE, 2 SLEEP, 3 BOTH (these are bit masks, not wire state IDs)
- exactly one qcom,use-voltage-corner or qcom,use-voltage-floor-corner
- regulator-min-microvolt and regulator-max-microvolt: logical bounds in1..7
Optional qcom,always-send-voltage preserves original disabled-client voltage
updates (used for floor requests). Disabled physical microvolt child nodes are
ignored. Parent supplies, boot-on and always-on requests are rejected: probe
must not guess a bootstrap corner or program power before clock ownership is
established. No init-voltage/default voltage is synthesized.

All stored logical requests aggregate by MAX per key and per set, including
requests from disabled frontends. SWEN aggregates independently; disabling a
client does not implicitly clear its stored corner. Higher-level clock users
must explicitly reduce their request after reducing/gating the hardware rate.

Unlike Sony's sleep-inheritance optimization, the first transmitted transaction
explicitly ACKs both owned ACTIVE and SLEEP keys. This does not depend on an
unknown bootloader sleep vote. ACTIVE-only requests therefore have an explicit
zero sleep-side vote when no BOTH/SLEEP consumer requests that key. Zero here
is a genuine apps-master release, not a fake power provider or guessed voltage.
All transport operations wait for native correlated firmware ACKs.

No hardware writes occur at probe or removal. Before the full resource is
registered, consumer mutations defer. Unknown physical voltage is reported as
ENODATA; is_enabled reports this frontend's logical request, not a PMIC read.

Clock coupling must set a source-derived logical corner, enable the consumer,
and call qcom_rpm_corner_sync(regulator, true) before enabling/raising a clock.
Generic regulator API cached success does not replace this explicit ACK.
The false argument permits disabled state confirmation, or an explicit
always-send voltage-only floor request; it is not proof of an enabled supply.

On partial failure, acknowledged old ACTIVE/SLEEP values are explicitly
restored. Failure to restore quarantines the resource. A failed initial
transaction with no ACK baseline holds max(previous request, attempted request)
and requires an explicit dominating retry; it never restores an assumed NONE
baseline. Returned errors preserve the first transaction failure. Uncertainty
is visible through REGULATOR_ERROR_FAIL and blocks cached/reducing success.
Source-derived bootstrap/ownership and caller failure sequencing are still
mandatory; this driver cannot infer the safe corner of unclaimed live clocks.

Suspend confirms both sets; unresolved uncertainty aborts suspend. Resume
re-confirms both sets and keeps further changes blocked if confirmation fails.
These software contracts do not establish physical suspend or voltage safety.

Exactly one resource frontend may own a given RPM transport/type/id tuple.
Callback storage remains alive until the last regulator device reference is
released. Provider removal marks all operations offline without blindly
withdrawing a voltage still required by live consumers.
